This might surprise you coming from someone who owns a shop that sells cleaning products…

But I don’t think you need a different cleaner for every room, every surface, or every mess.

In fact, I think that’s part of what makes cleaning feel so overwhelming.

Over the years, I’ve narrowed my routine down to a handful of trusted, multi-purpose products that I use again and again. They work, they’re easy to grab, and I never have to stand in my cleaning closet wondering which bottle to use.

That’s really what the Clean Mama Routine has always been about.

Not buying more or doing more, but making fewer decisions. When you remove the guesswork, it’s so much easier to stay consistent.

A simple routine.
A simple cleaning caddy.
A simple system.

That’s what keeps a home clean.

I know this one is going to be controversial. 😂

Years ago, I stopped using a top sheet, and honestly…I’ve never looked back.

Here’s why:

✨ It’s one less thing to wash every week.
✨ Making the bed takes less time.
✨ A duvet cover or washable quilt works better for my family and stays in place without the daily sheet battle.

For me, homekeeping is all about finding little ways to make everyday tasks easier.

It’s about creating routines and systems that work for your home.

If you love your top sheet, keep it! If you’ve been thinking about skipping it, this might be your sign to give it a try.

I know…this one might surprise some people but if you’ve been following along, I haven’t used it for over 20 years and it’s a big reason why Clean Mama is even here.

Most of the messes we’re cleaning are everyday dirt, dust, fingerprints, grease, soap scum, and spills. Those don’t usually require bleach or harsh chemicals to clean effectively.

Instead, I keep things simple with a few products I use over and over again:
✨ Hydrogen peroxide
✨ Oxygen Whitener ✨ Rubbing alcohol  ✨ Steam ✨ DIY cleaners made with vinegar or vodka ✨ Microfiber cloths

One of the biggest misconceptions about a clean home is that it has to smell like bleach to be clean. 
It doesn’t.
A clean home smells...clean.

The fewer products you own, the fewer decisions you have to make, and the easier it becomes to keep up with your routine. You can also find Clean Mama cleaning products in my shop - they’re simple and they WORK.

Do you have a weekly deep cleaning day? 👀

Here’s one of my biggest cleaning hot takes:

I don’t believe you need one.

If your entire house depends on one big cleaning day each week, missing that day can leave you feeling overwhelmed and behind before the next week even begins.

Instead, I divide my cleaning into simple Daily and Weekly Tasks.

✨ Monday: Bathrooms
✨ Tuesday: Dust
✨ Wednesday: Vacuum
✨ Thursday: Wash Floors
✨ Friday: Catch-All
✨ Saturday: Sheets & Towels
✨ Sunday: Daily Tasks

Each task takes just a little time, but together they keep your home clean all week long—without marathon cleaning sessions or trying to find an entire day to clean.

After more than 20 years of following this routine, I can honestly say I don’t have a “deep cleaning day.”

I have a system.

I haven’t had to decide when to wash my sheets and towels in over 20 years.
That might sound like a small thing, but it’s actually one of the biggest reasons the Clean Mama Routine works.
When you assign a Weekly Task to a specific day, you stop relying on memory, motivation, or guessing.

That’s one less decision to make, and one more thing your routine handles for you.
The goal isn’t to create more rules.
